title: C4: finiteness for constructible prime-to-char sheaves
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be a
smooth separated connected curve over $k$, let
$r$ be prime to $\operatorname{char}k$, and let the constant sheaf
$\mathbf F_r$ be viewed as a
constructible sheaf. Then
$\mathbf F_r$ satisfies $\mathcal C_4(C,\mathbf F_r)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]: $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)$
is a finite abelian group for every $q\geq0$.

proof.text: The underlying abelian sheaf of Λ/(r) is a finite biproduct of copies of constantZMod r: give the quotient its canonical ZMod r scalar action, lift scalars to ULift (ZMod r), take a basis, whose index is finite by injectivity into the finite quotient, and use the basis representation and the constant-sheaf/forgetting comparison. The empty basis handles the zero quotient. This coefficient argument is proved locally, without any new sorry.

In degree zero use the existing connected constant-sheaf H0 identification with ZMod r. For positive degree split on dim C = 1. The complementary case has dimension at most zero and its positive derived cohomology vanishes; the Ext/derived comparison transports this vanishing.

In dimension one form IsConnectedCurve f and apply the proper-or-affine dichotomy. In the proper case the explicit degree-one and degree-two coordinates are finite, and all higher groups vanish. In the affine case, the Kummer sequence identifies the kernel of β with the range of α; quotientKerEquivRange identifies that range with the finite units quotient. The range of β is the finite Picard torsion. AddMonoidHom.finite_iff_finite_ker_range proves H1 finite; all higher groups vanish.

Apply the additive cohomology functor to the coefficient biproduct isomorphism. Functor.mapBiproduct and AddCommGrpCat.biproductIsoPi identify the result with a finite product of finite prime-coefficient groups. Transport finiteness through that equivalence.
